A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IDIOMoE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments, language-retention evaluations, architectural ablations, representation analyses, and efficiency measurements in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds model-scaling, semantic-ID, and cold-start experiments in Appendix B.6.

M1.justification: Appendix B.6.2 adds an input variant replacing raw item IDs with semantic IDs from MQL4GRec. The core dual-FFN architecture, static routing, shared attention, and training objectives remain unchanged; the expanded routing description clarifies the existing method.

E1.justification: The datasets and language benchmarks are retained. v2 adds an unseen-item cold-start scenario on Arts, Games, and Instruments, extending evaluation beyond the previously reported recommendation setting. Larger backbones and semantic-ID encoding do not introduce additional datasets or domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, and the new scaling and semantic-ID experiments reuse Item-LLM. However, Table 11 labels its cold-start comparator only as Backbone without establishing whether it matches an existing trained comparator. A distinct comparator addition cannot be determined reliably.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. Added experiments introduce a Qwen 2.5 size sweep from 0.5B to 7B, semantic-ID inputs, and a cold-start protocol withholding 5% of test items from training, reporting overall and unseen-item metrics, and setting the unseen-to-seen recommendation ratio to 0.1.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 adds substantive analyses of backbone scaling, sensitivity to item encoding, and generalization to unseen items through Figure 6 and Tables 10–11. These address questions beyond v1's retained capacity, placement, routing, neuron-specialization, attention, and efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures. The added experiments report point results; existing graphical reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are unchanged, including the efficiency table renumbered from 10 to 12. v2 adds results across model sizes, semantic IDs, and cold-start conditions. Table 10 reports Arts HR@10 of 0.1018 for IDIOMoE versus 0.0946 for Item-LLM. Cold-start results mostly favor IDIOMoE, but Table 11 shows lower unseen-Arts HR@10: 0.0547 versus 0.0569. These are new experimental results, not revisions to v1's scores.

T1.justification: The FFN key-value formulation and affinity, purity, and clustered-row definitions in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about separating item and language processing, recommendation performance, language preservation, and expert specialization. Renaming Oral-language to Natural-language and adding supporting experiments do not change these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.1 newly acknowledges that MoA/MoT can outperform IDIOMoE on Amazon-Beauty and that the preferred expert architecture may be dataset-dependent. Appendix B.6 also extends the applicability discussion to semantic IDs and cold-start handling, supported by the new experiments.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added experiments' backbone sizes, semantic-ID source, withheld-item fraction, and recommendation ratio. Appendix B.6.4 newly clarifies that evaluations use batches larger than one and require no online adaptation beyond a forward pass. Existing optimization, hardware, freezing, and warm-up details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 and Appendix A.4 substantially broaden the literature discussion to multimodal MoE models, including MoE-LLaVA, Uni-MoE, and MoME, with additional references. However, the new multimodal MoME description conflicts with the retained Xu et al. bibliography entry, titled Mixture-of-masked-experts for efficient multi-task recommendation.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory expansions, adds related-work and appendix subsections plus acknowledgments, changes Oral-language to Natural-language, and updates the publication header and an author footnote. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the scaling plot in Figure 6 and semantic-ID/cold-start Tables 10–11, slightly reformats Figure 2, and adjusts table placement and text wrapping. Existing attention figures and the efficiency table are relocated and renumbered, with their content retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper through new scalability and new-item evaluations and a better-qualified interpretation of the MoA/MoT comparison. These additions support broader applicability while preserving the original evidence. Their benefit is limited by the underidentified cold-start comparator and unchanged uncertainty reporting, while the expanded related work introduces a MoME citation mismatch. Overall, the evidence and qualifications provide a modest net improvement.
